name: Ball Control
description: Toe taps and sole rolls between two cones to make the ball feel part of your feet.
steps: Set two cones 4 m apart. Stand halfway between them with the ball at your feet.
Toe taps: tap the top of the ball with your right sole, then your left, as fast as you can stay in control, for 30 seconds.
Sole roll: roll the ball sideways across your body with the sole of one foot, stop it with the inside of the other, and keep rolling until you reach one cone.
Roll it all the way back to the other cone leading with the other foot, then back to the first. That is one rep.
Do 3 rounds of 30 seconds toe taps + 4 reps of sole rolls. Rest 30 seconds between rounds.
coachingPoint: Stay on the balls of your feet with light touches on the top of the ball, never your heel.
cue: Light touches, stay on your toes
filmLabels: Sole roll across to the cone
All the way back, other foot leads
Reset in the middle, next round

name: Juggling
description: Keep the ball in the air with your feet and thighs and beat your record.
steps: Hold the ball at waist height, drop it onto your laces and kick it back up to your hands. Do this 10 times on each foot.
Now let it bounce once between touches: foot, bounce, foot. Go for 10 in a row.
Take the bounce away: juggle right foot, left foot, as many as you can. Count out loud.
When it drops, pick it up and start again. Juggle for 5 minutes and remember your best run.
Finish with 1 minute of thigh juggles, then try a run that mixes foot and thigh.
coachingPoint: Lock your ankle with your toes pointed slightly up so the ball comes straight back to you.
cue: Lock the ankle, small kicks to waist height
filmLabels: Lock the ankle, kick to waist height

name: Dribbling Cones
description: Weave through a line of cones with small touches, then turn and race back.
steps: Set 5 cones in a straight line, 2 m apart. Start 2 m before the first cone with the ball.
Weave through all 5 cones using the inside and outside of your right foot only. One touch between each pair of cones.
After the last cone, stop the ball with your sole, turn, and dribble straight back outside the line to the start.
Do 6 runs right foot only, 6 runs left foot only, then 6 runs using both feet as fast as you can.
Rest 30 seconds after every 3 runs. If you knock a cone over, that run does not count.
coachingPoint: Keep the ball within one step of you and glance up at the next cone before each touch.
cue: Small touches, eyes up between cones
filmLabels: Small touch to the first cone
Turn and race back outside the line
Back to the start, go again

name: Shooting Practice
description: Set up the ball with one touch and strike it low into the corners.
steps: Place a cone 14 m from the goal (11 m if you are under 12). Start with the ball 2 m behind the cone.
Push the ball past the cone with one setup touch, then strike it with your laces into a bottom corner.
Alternate corners: left, right, left. Call the corner out loud before you shoot.
Collect the ball and dribble back to the start at a jog. That jog is your rest. If you have more balls, line them up at the start.
Do 3 sets of 8 shots: right foot, left foot, then your choice. Count how many hit the target.
coachingPoint: Plant your standing foot beside the ball pointing at the corner, and keep your knee over the ball to keep the shot low.
cue: Plant, lock the ankle, strike through the middle
equipment: A goal (or two cones as posts by a fence)
space: 16 x 10 m in front of a goal

name: Passing Accuracy
description: Pass against a wall and take your first touch across your body before the next pass.
steps: Stand 5 m from a flat wall with the ball. Pick one brick or spot on the wall as your target.
Pass into the wall with the inside of your right foot.
As it comes back, take your first touch with your right foot across your body, about one step to your left.
Pass with your left foot, then touch the next one back across to your right. Keep going: touch, pass, touch, pass.
Do 4 rounds of 1 minute with 30 seconds rest. In round 4, pass one-touch with no control touch.
coachingPoint: Point your standing foot at the wall and strike through the middle of the ball with your ankle locked.
cue: Ankle locked, follow through to the target
space: 6 x 3 m in front of a wall

name: Sprint Training
description: Short, full-speed sprints with a walk back, the way you accelerate in a game.
steps: Warm up first: 3 minutes of easy jogging, then 10 leg swings on each leg.
Set a start cone, a cone 10 m away and a third cone 20 m from the start.
Stand just behind the start cone. Sprint flat out past the 10 m cone, then walk back to the start. Do 6 sprints.
Now sprint the full 20 m and walk back. Do 4 sprints.
Rest at least 30 seconds between sprints. If you are slowing down a lot, stop: speed work only helps at full speed.
coachingPoint: Drive your arms hard and push the ground back with short, quick steps for the first 5 m.
cue: Drive the arms, quick first steps
filmLabels: Walk back, that is your rest

name: Agility Ladder
description: Quick-feet patterns through a ladder, then a sprint out to a cone.
steps: Lay a ladder flat, or make one with 9 sticks or lines 45 cm apart. Put a cone 5 m past the end.
One foot in each square: run through as fast as you can without touching a rung.
Two feet in each square: right, left in every square.
Side shuffle: face sideways and step both feet into each square.
After each pattern, sprint out to the cone and walk back. Do each pattern 4 times.
coachingPoint: Stay on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent and pump your arms with your feet.
cue: Quick feet, stay on your toes

name: Endurance Run
description: Steady laps of a square with the ball to build stamina and touch at the same time.
steps: Mark a 15 x 15 m square with 4 cones.
Dribble round the outside of the square at a steady pace, a speed where you could still talk.
Every lap, change direction and switch feet: clockwise with the right foot, anticlockwise with the left.
On the last side of every third lap, push the ball ahead and run faster to the corner cone, then settle back to steady.
Do 3 blocks of 4 minutes with 1 minute of walking between blocks.
coachingPoint: Keep a steady pace you can hold for the whole block; push the ball a step ahead so you can run, not shuffle.
cue: Steady pace, push the ball and run
filmLabels: Steady pace down the first side
Push the ball ahead and run

name: 1v1 Practice
description: Attack a defender and dribble through either gate. Needs a partner.
steps: You need a partner. Make two small gates (2 m wide) at one end of a 15 x 12 m area.
The attacker starts with the ball at the far end. The defender starts 5 m in front of the gates.
The attacker dribbles at the defender and tries to get through either gate with the ball. Everything after the first touch is live.
The defender wins by stealing the ball or kicking it out. Walk the ball back after each go.
Swap roles after every 3 attacks. First to 5 points wins; play 3 games.
coachingPoint: Attack the defender's front foot at speed, then change pace the moment they commit.
cue: Go at their front foot, then explode
filmLabels: Beat them to the left gate
Or beat them to the right gate

name: Small-Sided Games
description: 2v2 up to 4v4 to small goals: pass, move and make quick decisions. Needs 4 to 8 players.
steps: You need 4 to 8 players. Mark a 20 x 15 m pitch with a small goal (2 m wide, two cones) at each end.
Split into two equal teams. One team kicks off from the middle; no goalkeepers.
Score by passing or dribbling the ball through the other team's goal.
When the ball goes out, the other team restarts with a pass from the line.
Play 4 games of 4 minutes with 1 minute rest. Change teams after each game.
coachingPoint: After you pass, move to a new space so your teammate always has someone to pass to.
filmLabels: Team A on the ball, Team B defends
Pass, and the nearest defender presses
